competitive_position.basis: Stated in the cited items (20-F Item 4.B Market Overview and Item 3.D Risk Factors).
competitive_position.claim: Trade protectionism and US–China tariffs disrupted LPG trade flows in 2025, nearly eliminating US–China LPG trade and forcing rerouting to Japan, Southeast Asia and India, with retaliatory tariffs suspended only in late 2025.
quotes: In early April, trade tensions between the US and China increased sharply as the two countries began imposing tariffs on each other. An increase in protectionism, trade disputes and the introduction of or increases to existing tariffs could have a material adverse impact on global trade, the shipping industry and the Group's business and materially adversely affect the Group's results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

The cash dividend is NOK8.8914 per share for shareholders receiving the dividend in NOK and US$0.95 per share for shareholders receiving the dividend in USD.

material_events.claim: BW LPG successfully placed an offering of USD 300 million senior unsecured convertible bonds due 2031 at a fixed coupon of 2.25% per annum, with net proceeds to partly finance a newbuild program for eight Panamax VLGCs with Hyundai Heavy Industries.
quotes: has today successfully placed an offering (the "Offering") of USD 300 million senior unsecured convertible bonds due 2031 (the "Bonds") convertible into new shares (the "Shares") of the Company.
The Company intends to use the net proceeds to partly finance the newbuild program with Hyundai Heavy Industries for eight Panamax VLGCs, and for general corporate purposes.

risks.basis: stated in P3 (operating results), P2 (risk factors), P1 (market overview); Q2 2026 recovery stated in P5
risks.claim: The highly cyclical LPG shipping market exposed BW LPG to a sharp decline in TCE per available day, falling from US$48,300 in 2024 to US$45,010 in 2025, driven by a 10.9% decline in average LPG spot rates during the US–China trade war.
quotes: TCE income — Shipping per available day for the entire fleet was US$45,010 per day for the year ended 31 December 2025, a decrease of 6.8% from US$48,300 per day for the year ended 31 December 2024.
In 2025, 69.3% of the Group's revenue from LPG shipping were generated on the basis of current market levels ("spot prices") and 30.7% of the Group's revenue were generated under time charters.

the short-term VLGC TCE rates for shipping LPG between the Middle East and Japan fluctuated between a high of US$175,874 per day to a low of US$6,243 per day from 2019 to the period ended 31 December 2025

risks.basis: stated in P5 (VLGC trade flows and market reactions section) and P2 (risk factors on geopolitical events)
risks.claim: The Strait of Hormuz remained closed in H1 2026 due to the armed conflict between the US, Israel and Iran, causing an approximate 46% year-on-year decline in Middle East LPG export growth and vessels idling in the Arabian Sea.
quotes: Exports remain heavily restricted as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed
Vessels idling in the Arabian Sea
The recent armed conflict between the United States, Israel and its allies and Iran has led to severe disruption and an effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz

risks.basis: stated in P1 (fleet overview and market overview) and P2 (risk factors on oversupply)
risks.claim: An oversupply of VLGC capacity is expected as 11 new VLGCs were delivered in 2025, the total fleet reached 413 vessels, and 2027 is expected to see a particularly high level of shipyard deliveries, which could depress freight rates.
quotes: The fleet continued its expansion, with 11 new VLGCs delivered in 2025, with the total fleet count at year end at 413.
Over the next three years, the VLGC fleet will see additional vessels being delivered from shipyards, with 2027 expected to see a particularly high level of deliveries.

If the supply of vessel capacity continues to increase and the demand for vessel capacity does not increase correspondingly, freight rates could materially decline and the value of the Group's vessels could be adversely affected.

risks.basis: stated in P5 (Q2 2026 financial results) and P3 (2025 annual results of operations)
risks.claim: Product Services experienced a non-cash unrealised mark-to-market loss of negative US$145 million in Q2 2026, producing a segment gross loss of US$18 million, and a further US$128.9 million decline in annual gross profit in 2025, exposing the company to significant earnings volatility from trading positions.
quotes: Reported trading results were a gross loss of US$18 million and a loss after tax of US$31 million, primarily due to a non-cash unrealised mark-to-market valuation change of negative US$145 million on open positions.
These factors collectively contributed to an decrease of US$128.9 million in gross profit for Product Services in the year ended 31 December 2025 compared to the prior year.

risks.basis: stated in F2 (income statement), P3 (MD&A on interest rate fluctuations), P1 (fleet acquisition), P9 (bond issuance), P5 (liquidity and leverage), P6 (vessel sale)
risks.claim: Interest expense tripled from US$19,849 thousand in 2024 to US$53,046 thousand in 2025, driven by the US$1,050 million Avance Gas acquisition debt and approximately US$632 million of net floating-rate debt, increasing sensitivity to interest rate movements.
quotes: As of 31 December 2025, the Group's net interest-bearing floating rate debt was approximately US$632 million.
In August 2024, the Group entered into agreements to acquire 12 VLGCs from Avance Gas for a total consideration of US$1,050 million.

risks.basis: stated in P6 (BW Loyalty sale), P5 (subsequent events for BW Elm, BW Birch, BW Levant), P2 (risk factors), F1 (balance sheet), F2 (income statement)
risks.claim: The Group is actively selling older vessels (BW Loyalty, BW Elm, BW Birch, BW Levant) at prices the company characterises as equivalent to newbuilding prices, but vessel values can fluctuate substantially and impairment charges may arise if values fall below carrying amounts.
quotes: Selling the BW Loyalty at a price in the low US$80 million demonstrates the strength of the second-hand market and our ability to realise value from our fleet.
Sale of 2007-built BW Elm and BW Birch, both second-hand sales at a value equivalent to a newbuilding price of ~US$248 million.

Over time, vessel values may fluctuate substantially and this may result in impairment charges and the Group could also incur a loss if these values are lower at a time when the Group is attempting to dispose of a vessel.

increased trade in LPG and other segments such as ethane, containers and LNG could increase demand for canal transits and consequently transit costs
